"False" means not according to truth or fact; incorrect; for example, "He was arrested for giving a false name to the police."

Both words refer to something that is not genuine or true, making "false" the correct synonym.

The other options - genuine (authentic), spontaneous (unplanned), and spiritual (relating to the soul) do not match the meaning of "spurious".

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. He attended a event. The event was an important one.

B. He attended an event. A event was important.

C. He attended an event. The event was important.

D. He attended a event. An event was important.
questions.solution_en:
Option A: Incorrect.

The indefinite article 'a' is incorrectly used before "event," which starts with a vowel sound, requiring 'an' as "an" is used before vowel-sounding words, while "a" is used before consonant-sounding words. The second sentence correctly uses 'the event' but cannot compensate for the first error.

Option B: Incorrect.

'An event' is correct in the first sentence, but 'A event' in the second sentence is incorrect for the same reason as above.

Option C: Correct.

Both sentences use the correct articles: 'an event' for the first sentence and 'the event' for the specific event referenced in the second sentence.

Option D: Incorrect.

The first sentence repeats the error of using 'a event'. The second sentence is also incorrect because "an" fails to denote specificity.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

Dog trainers typically describe their training methods on their websites. The scientists analysed these training philosophies to identify the words and phrases used by trainers to indicate different methods. Because 56 percent were ambiguous, they also looked at the tools used and at reviews. They classified the trainers as non-aversive (i.e., reward-based) or aversive. 55 percent of the trainers were classed as aversive, meaning they used aversive methods at least some of the time. The results showed that some words or phrases were pretty much only used by one kind of trainer, and never or rarely by the other. The exception was sometimes when a non-aversive trainer mentioned that they did not use a particular method. Aversive trainers sometimes described a "balanced approach" while non-aversive trainers wrote about positive reinforcement. Some words were used by both types of trainers but in different ways; for example, when aversive trainers referred to "tools" they meant concrete things like shock collars, whereas non-aversive trainers more often used this word to describe skills or knowledge that the dog's guardian would develop. Some phrases seem to always indicate an aversive trainer: electronic or e-collar, pack leader, and mother nature. Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The minister told his associate that he had been playing to the gallery.
options_en: The minister said to his associate, "I played to the gallery."

The minister said to his associate, "I will play to the gallery."

questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were+V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said that he had been watching television the previous night. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I was watching television last night". (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect speech to Direct Speech:

told.. thatsaid to
heI
had been playingwas playing

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) The minister said to his associate, "I was playing to the gallery."

questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['being'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): A delicious three-course meal is being meticulously prepared by the talented chef for the guests. Meanwhile, the dining area is being efficiently set up by the staff to ensure a welcoming atmosphere for everyone involved.

questions.q_en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The gardener said to the children, "Please do not pluck any flowers."
options_en: The gardener requested to the children please do not pluck any flowers.
The gardener told to the children to kindly not pluck any flowers.
The gardener ordered the children to not pluck any flowers.
The gardener requested the children not to pluck any flowers.
questions.solution_en:
Imperative Sentences are used to demonstrate Request, Order, Command, etc.

Imperative Sentences begin with Principal verbs like Go, Make, etc.

The reporting verbs like "said", "say", etc. in direct speech are changed into "begged", "beg", etc.

"To" is used before the Principal Verbs in Indirect Speech.

For example:

John said to his assistant, "Bring me a glass of water." (Direct Speech)

John ordered his assistant to bring him a glass of water. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to' into 'requested'.

'Please do not' into 'not to'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The gardener requested the children not to pluck any flowers.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

"Say/ Said" in Direct Speech is changed into "Propose/ Proposed", "Suggest/ Suggested" etc.

If there is an object in Direct Speech, "to" is used after "proposed" and "suggested" in Indirect Speech.

Let as a proposal:

He said, "Let us go to the library" (Direct Speech)

He proposed that they should go to the library. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:
Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
saidproposed that
Let us movethey should move

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a) The man proposed that they should move to a new place.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 5 Questions]: Directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The population of Venice, more than 170,000 after the second world war, has ____________(A) steadily to some 52,000 today. Remaining residents still feel _______________(B) to live in a city of such beauty, many believing their culture survives despite the onslaught, but they also grieve at the losses, lose heart, and move away at a rate of 1,000 a year to homes on the mainland. A Venice without Venetians - without significant numbers of permanent residents - is ______________(C) for as early as 2030. It is no ________________(D) to say that mass tourism - adding to Venice's existing issues with mismanagement of the environment, corruption, political stasis and now the climate emergency - is bringing the community, the lagoon, and a fabulous heritage to within a ___________(E) of collapse.

Which of the following can fit in the blank E?
questions.solution_en: The given blank will take the phrase 'hair's breadth' (means 'a very small distance or margin') as the sentence says that tourism and the other issues in Venice all together moving it on the verge of collapse. Hence, the answer is option b).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

The old bookstore with its ________ wooden floors and shelves lined with ________ volumes, exuded a nostalgic charm that drew readers seeking solace in the ________ pages of classic literature.
questions.solution_en:
The words 'creaky, ancient, and weathered' appropriately describe an old bookstore with worn wooden floors and aged book volumes, enhancing the nostalgic atmosphere mentioned in the sentence.

'Creaky' means 'making or liable to make a creaking sound when being moved or when pressure is applied'.

'Weathered' means 'worn by long exposure to the atmosphere'.

'New' and 'modern' do not fit in contextually to explain 'volumes' (of books) in an old bookstore. 'Glossy' is not an appropriate adjective for books.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said, "I can distinguish a genuine antique from a reproduction."
options_en: He said that he could distinguish a genuine antique from a reproduction.
He said to me that he could distinguish a genuine antique from a reproduction.
He said that I could distinguish a genuine antique from a reproduction.
He said that he could be distinguished a genuine antique from a reproduction.
questions.solution_en:
When converting direct speech into indirect speech, the present modal verbs (can/may/must/will/shall) should be changed into past modal verbs (could/might/had to/would/should).

Example: She said, "I can speak ten languages." (Direct Speech)

She said that she could speak ten languages. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· 'Can' is changed into 'could'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): He said that he could distinguish a genuine antique from a reproduction.

questions.q_en:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the question that follows.

As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day but slows down in its activities after midday. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year. Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That's a question.

Choose the word which closely means 'adversely'.
questions.solution_en:
The word "adversely" in the passage is used in the context: "Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife," meaning hunting is having a harmful or negative impact. "Detrimentally" means causing harm or damage, which is a close synonym for "adversely."

(a) Distressing: Means causing emotional pain or upset, which is not the same as causing harm or negative impact in a general sense, as "adversely" implies here.

(b) Scarcely: Means barely or hardly, indicating scarcity or insufficiency, which is unrelated to harmful effects.

(d) Digressing: Means deviating or straying from a topic, which has no relation to causing harm or negative impact.

Hence, the correct answer is option (3).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the bracketed group of words.

He is a (person who talks too much).
questions.solution_en:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Taciturn: (of a person) reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little.

Garrulous: excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.

Generous: showing a readiness to give more of something, especially money, than is strictly necessary or expected.

Laconic: (of a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words.

Among the given options, 'garrulous' is the correct choice.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
